abstract: The Global Entrepreneurship Monitor (GEM) 2024/2025 Global Report surveys entrepreneurship rates, conditions, and attitudes across 50+ economies worldwide. Titled 'Entrepreneurship Reality Check,' the report provides baseline measures of early-stage entrepreneurial activity (TEA rates), established business ownership, and entrepreneurial intentions alongside assessments of national framework conditions for entrepreneurship. The GEM survey is the largest ongoing study of entrepreneurial dynamics globally and provides critical context for understanding whether AI-driven changes in labor markets are manifesting in entrepreneurship patterns. The report tracks both necessity entrepreneurship (driven by lack of alternatives) and opportunity entrepreneurship (driven by perceived market opportunities), a distinction that becomes particularly relevant as AI potentially displaces some workers into self-employment while creating new venture opportunities for others. Cross-country variation in entrepreneurship rates and conditions enables comparative analysis of how different institutional environments mediate AI's impact on new venture creation.
keyFindings: GEM tracks early-stage entrepreneurial activity (TEA) rates across 50+ economies, providing the most comprehensive global benchmark for entrepreneurship dynamics.

The report distinguishes between necessity entrepreneurship (lack of alternatives) and opportunity entrepreneurship (perceived market opportunities), a framework directly applicable to analyzing AI's dual displacement/creation effects.
Cross-country variation in entrepreneurship rates, conditions, and digital infrastructure enables comparative analysis of how institutional environments mediate technology-driven entrepreneurship.

National framework conditions for entrepreneurship (financing, government policy, education, R&D transfer) vary substantially across economies, creating different receptivity to AI-enabled venture creation.
The 2024/2025 report provides a pre-mature-AI-adoption baseline against which future shifts in entrepreneurship rates and composition can be measured.
methodology: Annual population survey (Adult Population Survey, APS) of at least 2,000 adults per participating economy, combined with a National Expert Survey (NES) of at least 36 experts per economy assessing entrepreneurship framework conditions. Covers 50+ economies across all income levels and regions. Standardized survey instruments enable cross-country and longitudinal comparisons. Published annually by the GEM consortium.
qualifiers: GEM measures self-reported entrepreneurial activity and intentions, which may not correspond to formal business registration data. The survey does not directly track AI-related entrepreneurship or technology adoption by entrepreneurs. Cross-country comparisons are complicated by different cultural understandings of entrepreneurship. The survey captures a snapshot and may miss rapid shifts in entrepreneurship driven by technology changes between survey waves. Not all economies participate in every survey wave, creating gaps in longitudinal coverage.
